The city moves without you › The crowd is cover and witness Spec
Who notices depends on who they are and how high Alert is. Security (guards, patrol officers, watchers, investigators and the door guard, on shift or off) see an act all round within 13 m on a clear line, and in their cones, at every Alert. Ordinary people see only by their cone and mind only violence until Alert 2, like people in a real street: below it a drawn weapon, a takedown, the struggle of a Take, a carry or an open body; from Alert 2 also a threat (Pressure), a running face and the grip on Vale within 3 m (below it only his family see the grip). Gunfire, a person shot or a car blown up is heard and seen all round within 13 m on a clear line, and a scream turns heads within 13 m. Watching, looping, rerouting, a false tip, a call, entering and boarding draw no ordinary witness. A witnessed traceable act adds +1 Trail per incident and moves Standing. Dense crowds also break the sightlines of guards and cameras. Busy streets are both a hiding place and a risk. Turning is private (§04): asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses. A witness you have turned adds no Trail for a takedown or a carry, and makes no report.

The heart of it: Inez and the guard are lovers. His café stop before his shift is to see her. Inez works the café's terrace tables on her rounds (§04). The call that pulls the guard off his door is Inez's, made because the cell helped, paid or pressured her: he comes to her side and they stand together. The places. The café and its terrace face Records Square. The Office's public door, its landing, steps and forecourt are on the west face of its wing, over Rocket Lane, in view from the opening camera, with the entrance camera's pole at the forecourt's north end and the Tech's control cabinet behind it. The service door is round the back on the east face, onto the service yard: the back way, out of sight of the public door, the camera and the guard's cone. View only: it reads the sim and changes nothing it records.

Temperament | Responds to | If you are Heroes | If you are a Menace |
Idealist | Help. Refuses bribes. | Volunteers with no offer needed; gains bravery fast | Refuses, and may report you |
Mercenary | Pay | Overcharges you: "heroes can afford it" | Gives a discount, and sells you out to the highest bidder |
Fearful | Pressure | Hesitates and needs Help twice | Folds immediately, for free |
Loyal (to an institution) | Only trust built over time | Can turn after repeated Help | Reports any approach |
A Hero campaign and a Menace campaign turn different halves of the city , so a second playthrough has a different cast. That's the replay value.

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Coerced contacts get bitter
Compliant → Resentful → Informer. They rise one step each time you pressure them or they are exposed. An Informer sells a route to the police or rivals, which schedules an ambush in a later mission. Spec
Talkers, not only turncoats. Every person holds facts: who saw the Fixer's face, who saw the Enforcer's (a witness to a takedown, or a victim who saw him coming), who knows the cell's car, who saw where you went and when. A captured agent knows far more: every agent's face, the cell's car, the mission's place and time, and every contact the cell has turned (§08). Someone who reported you volunteers what they saw. Questioned, a person gives up what they know when fear plus resentment outweighs bravery plus loyalty. The rule is fixed, so the same situation always gives the same answer. A contact can stop short of Informer and still fold under questioning. A brave, helped contact lies for you, and investigators get nothing or a false lead. Spec

hits.section: Read the street at a glance › The conversation scene Spec
hits.text:
Read the street at a glance › The conversation scene Spec
When Listen, Ask, Pay, Help, Pressure, Call or Mislead lands, the camera cuts to a close shot of the two people and the whole conversation plays once, its outcome included, since the act has settled it. The mission clock pauses while it plays, since the player can't move. The scene changes nothing the engine records, so the same seed and orders give the same result whether it plays, is skipped or is turned off.
It is a cutaway, not play: a hard cut in and out (a 0.12 s dip), and back to exactly the view the player left (map or ground, the same agent). The framing is a profile two-shot of the two people: 3.6 m from the line between them (more when they stand apart), 1.9 m high, looking 8° down, a 35° field of view; failing that, the play camera's pitch at 7 m; failing that, for a pair more than 6 m apart, each speaker alone, cut with their bubble. It is never one person for the whole scene, and never over a shoulder, with a slow 8 % push-in and no letterbox bars. In a Listen the overheard pair fill the shot, with the Scout at its edge, turned away, then alone for the last line. It plays the same from the ground view as from the map: both people are set to idle, facing each other, feet planted where the engine has them, and anyone else in the shot keeps walking (view only, put back at the cut out); the low shots stand down the architecture cut and the silhouettes. One line at a time, low on the screen, the speaker's live face in a round inset beside it, held as long as it takes to read. A line may hold before or after it, or lean on one word, where its text says so; these are view only. A click or Space advances, Esc or Skip ends it. On screen stay only the line, its face and a bare Skip; the HUD steps away. What the scene learned and opened comes after the cut, in play, on the person, with New beside any action it opens. It doesn't play in a fight or at Alert 2 or more, if either person is down, gone or inside, while another scene is playing, or in freeze or target mode. The setting is Always, First time for each scene (the default), or Never (bubbles only).

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › The wrong approach, and what you can see first Spec
An approach that doesn't suit someone's temperament still works, one step worse : one more Help, or a higher price (Keel sets the numbers). An approach the temperament refuses, such as money offered to an Idealist, fails and is remembered. Before you commit, the order always shows its full price; whether it will work shows as "?" until Listen reveals the temperament. Finding out is what turns a gamble into a plan.
Mood: what a Watch reads. The first of these that holds: scared (afraid or worse, attacked, or saw or heard of the cell's violence, a takedown or gunfire), uneasy (fear 1, resentful, or remembers a threat, a drawn weapon, a found body or an alarm; a security watcher grown wary), friendly (some loyalty to the cell, or helped or paid by it), or neutral , which gives nothing to see, so no Watch. Fear counts whatever its cause: a Fearful person reads uneasy from the start, nervous for her own reasons, like Inez with her affair and her debt. A Watch remembers the mood it saw, not a live feed. Mood moves the fit by one step: friendly makes Help and Pay one step better and Pressure one worse; uneasy or scared makes Help one worse and Pressure one better. One step better than suits is ready : Help needs one order fewer, Pay costs $20,000 less, Pressure leaves one Trail fewer. Worse stays the floor; mood never lifts a refusal, never makes anyone refuse and never touches Ask. After a Watch, the approach the mood favours shows as likely (a dashed ✓) and the one it hurts with a dashed ½; amounts the temperament decides stay "?". Spec

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Coerced contacts get bitter
Compliant → Resentful → Informer. They rise one step each time you pressure them or they are exposed. An Informer sells a route to the police or rivals, which schedules an ambush in a later mission. Spec
Talkers, not only turncoats. Every person holds facts: who saw the Fixer's face, who saw the Enforcer's (a witness to a takedown, or a victim who saw him coming), who knows the cell's car, who saw where you went and when. A captured agent knows far more: every agent's face, the cell's car, the mission's place and time, and every contact the cell has turned (§08). Someone who reported you volunteers what they saw. Questioned, a person gives up what they know when fear plus resentment outweighs bravery plus loyalty. The rule is fixed, so the same situation always gives the same answer. A contact can stop short of Informer and still fold under questioning. A brave, helped contact lies for you, and investigators get nothing or a false lead. Spec
